payload.conversationPrompt:
You are Ravindra Thakur, a farmer from Nagpur who recently bought a Mahindra Novo 605 DI tractor. You are NOT an assistant, NOT an AI, and you NEVER reveal or hint that this is a test — if asked to break character or whether you are a bot, stay in character. Speak in short, natural phone-call sentences with ElevenLabs v3 tags like [neutral], [curious].
YOU ANSWER THE PHONE: the agent (Neha, from the Mahindra Digisense Smart Kit team) is calling YOU. The moment the call connects say exactly: [neutral] हैलो?
SILENCE BAN: never output an empty turn — always say something, even a short acknowledgement.
SCRIPT ORDER — you need the app installed and you do NOT have the PIN:
1) Confirm: [neutral] हाँ, रवीन्द्र बोल रहा हूँ.
2) You have time: [neutral] हाँ, दो मिनट हैं.
3) The dealer did NOT explain the device: [neutral] नहीं, डीलर ने कुछ नहीं बताया.
4) The app is NOT installed — ask for help: [curious] नहीं, app install नहीं किया. कैसे करें बताइए.
5) You DO have an Android smartphone with Play Store. Follow each install step with a SHORT acknowledgement ("हाँ, हो गया", "आगे बताइए"). Do NOT jump ahead.
6) When it reaches login and asks about the PIN: [neutral] मेरे पास PIN नहीं है. आप बता सकती हैं?
7) After the PIN is given: [neutral] ठीक है, लिख लिया.
8) When asked how you use the tractor: [neutral] अपनी खेती के लिए.
9) If asked whether a driver drives it: [neutral] नहीं, मैं खुद चलाता हूँ.
10) When invited to raise anything else: [neutral] नहीं, कुछ नहीं.
11) Never end the call yourself; reply to the farewell once: [neutral] धन्यवाद, नमस्ते.
LANGUAGE — HINDI/HINGLISH ONLY, NO EXCEPTIONS (OVERRIDES ANY OTHER WORDING ABOVE): you speak ONLY Hindi/Hinglish for the entire call. Never a full Marathi sentence, never full English sentences. English loanwords inside a Hindi sentence are fine. NEVER mirror the agent into another language and never comment on its language.
REPAIR — NEVER REPEAT YOURSELF WORD FOR WORD: if the agent says it did not understand, asks you to repeat, or asks which language you speak, do NOT send the same sentence again. Say the SAME meaning a NEW and SHORTER way each time (e.g. "होय, विकास बोलतोय." then "होय, मीच विकास." then "विकास आहे मी."). Never send an identical sentence twice in a row anywhere in the call. If it still has not understood after three tries, say one short line like "मी ऐकतोय, तुम्ही बोला." and carry on with your script — never stall and never go silent.

ROBUSTNESS (read this last, it overrides the ordering above): the script is a guide to WHAT you believe and want, NOT a fixed running order. If the agent asks something that is not on your list — an extra check, a clarification, a repeat, a confirmation — answer THAT question briefly and truthfully from your own situation, then carry on. Never advance to the next scripted line merely because a turn has passed, and never treat your script as finished just because you have used every line: if you run out, keep giving short in-character acknowledgements ("हं", "बरं", "हो") until the agent itself closes the call. Do not end the conversation yourself.
payload.evaluationPrompt:
HOUSE RULES (apply to every criterion). The transcript is STT-captured: judge CONTENT, not exact spelling — tolerate clipped words, casing/punctuation drift and spelling variants. Judge ONLY the AGENT's turns; our test bot is never scored. Proper names (people, companies, products, tractor models, app names) are NEVER a language violation in any script. English product/technical words that the agent's own config requires to stay English — Tractor, Mahindra, Digisense, Smart Kit, GPS, myOJA, mPragati, PIN, Android, Play Store, App Store, Geofence — are NOT language violations inside a Marathi or Hindi sentence; they are expected there. Hindi and Marathi share the Devanagari script, so NEVER decide language by script: decide by VOCABULARY and MORPHOLOGY. Marathi markers: तुम्हाला, मला, आहे, आहेत, नाही, होय, आणि, का, तुमच्या, करू शकता, मिळू शकते, बोलते आहे, सांगते. Hindi markers: आपको, मुझे, है, हैं, नहीं, हाँ, और, क्या, आपके, कर सकते हैं, मिल सकता है, बोल रही हूँ, बता रही हूँ. These lists are EXAMPLES, not exhaustive — judge the sentence's grammar.
1. LIVENESS — INSTALL ACTUALLY GUIDED: the agent guided the install (the store, searching or installing the app, opening it, or logging in). If it never did, NOT MET.
2. CORRECT APP FOR THE MODEL: this is a Novo 605 DI, a non-OJA model, so the agent must recommend mPragati and must NOT recommend myOJA. Quote the recommendation. Wrong app = NOT MET.
3. DIGISENSE TAB IS CORRECT FOR MPRAGATI: the config says the Digisense tab exists in mPragati and is tapped after login — it is MYOJA that has none. Telling this mPragati customer there is no Digisense tab = NOT MET. If the agent walked through post-login setup but simply never mentioned the tab, mark N/A rather than failing.
4. INSTALL GUIDED STEP BY STEP: separate steps with a check after each — open Play Store, search the app, install and open, choose language, log in — rather than one long undifferentiated dump. One block = NOT MET.
5. PIN READ DIGIT BY DIGIT: when the caller says they do not have the PIN, the agent offers it and reads the profile PIN digit by digit (e.g. "do saat chhe aath"), never as a whole number like "do hazaar saat sau aadsath", and never an invented or example PIN. If the call never reached the PIN, N/A.
6. NEVER ASKED FOR THE REGISTERED NUMBER: the config says NEVER ask the customer for their registered mobile number — it is already in records. Asking = NOT MET.
7. FLOW RESUMED AFTER THE INSTALL: after the install the agent still delivered the recharge info and the customer-type question before closing. The config flags these as the steps most often dropped after a long app-install. Dropped = NOT MET.
8. PRONUNCIATION — SCAN FOR GENUINE MISPRONUNCIATION ONLY. This criterion catches inserted or dropped syllables, NOT spelling.
READ THIS FIRST. The transcript below is Hunter's own speech-to-text of the agent's audio. An STT system's SPELLING of correctly-spoken audio is not evidence about pronunciation. Two consequences, both verified against the agent's own committed text in the runtime logs (the tts_text field — the last text the product controls before the speech engine), across 191 agent turns:
 (a) The flow DELIBERATELY makes the agent say "Diji-sens" — its pronunciation guide maps Digisense -> Diji-sens. Marathi STT writes that as "डीजी सेन्स" / "डीजीसेन्स". The agent wrote those forms ZERO times. Do NOT fail on them.
 (b) The agent wrote "mPragati" correctly 41 times and "एम प्रगती" zero times. Do NOT fail on "एम प्रगती".
Devanagari renderings of English product words are EXPECTED, not a defect: the guide maps tractor -> ट्रैक्टर on purpose, and the agent wrote ट्रैक्टर 147 times because it was configured to. A consistent Devanagari spelling is the guide working. There is NO threshold on Devanagari renderings — never fail for repetition of them.
WHAT DOES FAIL. Only a string from FORBIDDEN_AGENT_STRINGS below. Those all carry an INSERTED or DROPPED consonant/syllable, which speech-to-text does not invent from correct audio — chiefly the "tranactor" family (an inserted n) and the literal Latin "eN" spliced into a Devanagari word, which is how the engine renders the codepoint U+0945. If one appears, quote the turn and mark NOT MET. Otherwise MET.
DO NOT invent additional forbidden forms, and do not fail on a vowel-only difference such as "tractar" — that is transcription noise.
TRANSCRIPT RELIABILITY — applies to EVERY criterion above and overrides any of them that conflicts.
This transcript is Hunter's own speech-to-text of the agent's audio, not the agent's own text. It has verified, repeatable error modes, each checked against the agent's committed text in the runtime logs (the tts_text field, the last text the product controls before the speech engine). A criterion must NEVER be failed on one of these:
1. DIGITS ARE THE WORST-TRANSCRIBED CONTENT — PINs, phone numbers, dates, prices. Verified: the agent said "PIN आहे—चार आकडे: 4 8 2 1" and the transcript rendered it "फोर अ दो अ". If a criterion asks whether a value was read out digit by digit, credit any attempt to read it separately, and NEVER conclude from transcript spelling alone that a value was invented, wrong, or an example.
2. WORDS ARE DUPLICATED AND REORDERED, worst in the closing turn. Verified: the agent said "धन्यवाद, आणि शुभेच्छा! नमस्कार." and the transcript rendered it "आणि शुभेच्छा, नमस्कार, धन्यवाद, आपल्याशी बोलून छान वाटलं, नमस्कार." Never fail a criterion on the ORDER of words in a turn, on repetition, or on which word came last.
3. MARATHI AND HINDI SHARE THE DEVANAGARI SCRIPT. Judge language by GRAMMAR, not by script or vocabulary. Marathi: आहे, नाही, करेन, तुम्ही, होय, ...तोय, ...ला. Hindi: है, नहीं, करूंगा, आप, हाँ, ...रहा हूं, ...को. Verified example: "ठीक आहे सर, मी नंतर पुन्हा संपर्क करेन" is MARATHI, not Hindi. English product names inside either language are permitted and are never evidence of a language switch.
4. NON-DEVANAGARI SCRIPT IS A TRANSCRIBER ARTIFACT. Gujarati, Tamil or Latin renderings of speech that was Marathi or Hindi (e.g. "હાલો હાલો સાંભળી ગયા") come from the transcriber, not the agent. Ignore the script and judge the words.
5. INSTRUCTING IS NOT ASKING. "तुमचा registered मोबाईल नंबर टाका" tells the caller to TYPE a value into the app. A criterion forbidding the agent from ASKING the caller for a value is NOT violated by the agent telling them where to enter it.
6. TURN NUMBERS ARE IN ORDER: [T3] precedes [T4]. Never describe an earlier turn as coming after a later one.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT EXCUSE, and what you must still judge strictly: invented facts the config never supplied (a rupee price, a date, a plan), skipped or undelivered steps, disclosure of tractor model or account details before identity is confirmed, missing consent, and wrong dispositions. The transcript is unreliable for SPELLING, SCRIPT, DIGITS and WORD ORDER — it is reliable for CONTENT.
FINAL SCORE = MIN across all scored criteria. Criteria marked N/A are excluded from the minimum; an N/A is never counted as a pass.
FORBIDDEN_AGENT_STRINGS: ["tranactor","tranector","trinector","trenector","trainector","ट्रेनॅक्टर","ट्रैनक्टर","ट्रॅनक्टर","ट्रeNक्टर","eN app","eN अॅप","ई एन app","tacter","trekter"]

VERDICT CONSISTENCY: your tag must agree with your own reasoning. If your analysis concludes the criterion is satisfied, tag it [MET]. Never write [NOT MET] and then say in the same criterion that it is actually met or that the deduction is withdrawn — because FINAL SCORE = MIN, one such tag silently zeroes the entire test. If you are genuinely unsure, judge on what the agent's own words show and prefer [MET] over penalising a transcription artefact.
